articles.title: Chamari Athapaththu’s 83 sinks Pakistan as Sri Lanka chase down 178 target to reach Asian Games final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a matc.
articles.body: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a match-winning knock to guide her side to an eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in the first semi-final on Sunday.Chasing 178 at Korogi Sports Park, Sri Lanka reached 178/2 in 17.5 overs, sealing the win with 13 balls to spare. The victory guarantees Sri Lanka at least a silver medal, while Pakistan will compete in the bronze-medal match.Pakistan post competitive totalAfter a delayed start, Pakistan recovered from an early setback through a strong partnership between Ayesha Zafar and Shawaal Zulfiqar. Zafar led the charge with an aggressive 71 off 40 balls, while Zulfiqar contributed 54 off 50 deliveries. The pair added 115 runs to put Pakistan in a strong position before the team finished its 20 overs at 177/4.Athapaththu leads Sri Lanka’s emphatic chaseSri Lanka’s chase was anchored by Athapaththu, who struck an unbeaten 83 off 50 balls. Her innings featured seven boundaries and six sixes as she took control of the contest after settling in. Imesha Dulani added 26 off 21 balls, helping Sri Lanka maintain momentum, while the captain continued to attack the Pakistan bowlers and guide her team towards the target.Pakistan struggled to contain Sri Lanka, with their bowling and fielding unable to halt the scoring. Sri Lanka eventually completed the chase in 17.5 overs, losing just two wickets.The win sends Sri Lanka into the gold-medal match, where they will face the winner of the second semi-final between India and Bangladesh. Pakistan, meanwhile, will take on the losing side in the bronze-medal playoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana creates history in Asain Games semi-final, becomes leading run-scorer in Women's T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved th.
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved the milestones during a blistering start against Bangladesh, as India raced to 71/1 in the powerplay in their bid to book a place in the gold-medal match.India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first in the second semi-final. Mandhana and Shafali Verma provided an explosive start, putting Bangladesh’s bowlers under pressure from the outset.Mandhana surpasses Suzie BatesMandhana struck 37 off just 19 deliveries, hitting five fours and two sixes before her innings ended in the final over of the powerplay. She attempted another slog sweep off Nahida Akter but mistimed the shot, with Sobhana Mostary completing the catch at deep mid-wicket.Despite her dismissal, Mandhana had already etched her name in the record books, moving past New Zealand’s Suzie Bates to become the leading run-scorer in women’s T20Is. She also became the first Indian woman to reach 100 sixes in the format.Most runs in Women’s T20IsPlayerRunsSmriti Mandhana4,788Suzie Bates4,758Harmanpreet Kaur4,287Chamari Athapaththu4,282Sophie Devine3,817India make a flying startShafali joined Mandhana in attacking Bangladesh’s bowling, helping India reach 71/1 in the first six overs. The opening stand gave India early momentum in a high-stakes contest, with a place in the gold-medal match on the line.Playing XIs for India Women vs Bangladesh Women in the Asain Games Semi-finalIndia Women: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Gunalan Kamalini, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Richa Ghosh (wk), Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Shree Charani, Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud.Bangladesh Women: Dilara Akter, Juairiya Ferdous, Sobhana Mostary, Nigar Sultana (wk/c), Shorna Akter, Sharmin Akhter, Shanjida Akter Meghla, Rabeya Khan, Nahida Akter, Marufa Akter, Sultana Khatun.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How one India T20I could become Japanese cricket's defining moment
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Associ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Association (JCA) COO pulled covers off the wicket. Later, he was putting up hospitality tents, checking security plans and helping transform a quaint cricket ground with 500 permanent seats into a venue worthy of hosting the reigning T20I world champions. By Tuesday, weather permitting, India will walk out against Japan in the country's first-ever men's senior international against a Full Member.For Japanese cricket, getting here is success in itself and the scoreline almost secondary."A lot of success has almost already happened," Curr says. "The fact that India have agreed to come, the fact that I'm sitting here talking to you guys, the fact that Japanese media are coming to learn about cricket — we're having successes already," he told select media.Cricket is not new to Japan, having been introduced in the 1870s. But adaptation is a different story. Baseball, Football, Sumo Wrestling, Basketball, Golf, Tennis, Boxing are some sports that are bigger. India's arrival represents cricket's loudest introduction in recent memory.More than just another T20I matchJapan has played in Under-19 World Cups, faced India and Pakistan at youth level and competed in the Asian Games with its women's team. But this is different gravy."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan," Curr says. "It's piquing interest, but we've still got a long way to go before cricket breaks into the mainstream sporting audience."That mainstream audience is precisely what the JCA hopes to reach. The timing is ideal: cricket returns to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya just days later, allowing Japan to explain the sport through one of the country's most recognisable sporting events."The Asian Games gives cricket legitimacy that it didn't have before," Curr says. "You can't be what you can't see."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan.Cricket's quiet, but slow, growth in JapanBehind the scenes, cricket has been expanding steadily in Japan. Registered players have risen from around 3,000 when Curr arrived in 2014 to 8,800 today. The Japan Cup -- the T20 competition in the country -- has grown from barely a dozen teams to more than 80, while the domestic 40-over league now spans four divisions."Kaizen is the word," Curr says. "Continual improvement. That's what we're trying to do for the sport. But now and again there are moments like this where you can accelerate that," he added.Winning hearts and viewers, not necessarily the matchJapan harbour no illusions about the cricketing challenge ahead. "This India team is pretty good," Curr said as a matter of fact. "It's going to be an extremely difficult challenge for players who have never played at that level before."Instead, his measure of success is cultural.He points to Japan's women's team, praised recently for staying back after their Asian Games fixture against India to thank supporters and mingle with fans. That's the identity he wants the men's side to showcase too."We want cricket to be played hard but also be accessible and friendly," he says. "We want cricket to be fun."If thousands of first-time spectators leave Sano remembering more than just India's star power, Japanese cricket may have achieved exactly what it came for.The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCAHow India fixture came into beingThe historic fixture was never part of Japan's grand plan to expand the sport. It began with clay.Eighteen months ago, the JCA set out to relay the turf square at Sano with help from Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), whose groundsman travelled to Japan to identify suitable clay. The same surface was eventually used to build the Asian Games venue in Nagoya, prompting a simple thought: if Japan had international-quality wickets, why not invite the world's best teams to use them?Once the pitches were completed in March, Japan prepared a proposal and sent it to every Full Member ahead of the ICC conference in Edinburgh. Conversations with the BCCI began there — and, to Curr's surprise, moved quickly."The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCA," he said.The timing made sense. With the Asian Games beginning days later, India men's squad would otherwise spend nearly a week waiting for their knockout fixture without access to proper cricket facilities. Sano offered both a training base and, eventually, a match. Again, with fingers crossed that the weather doesn't play spoilsport.India vs Japan T20I will be broadcast LIVE on FanCode on September 22 at 9:30 am IST.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI to draw line on Ombudsman’s jurisdiction over state-level matters | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office from entertaining complaints concerning local or state-level matters, the TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The move is understood to aim at drawing a clearer line between issues that fall within the Ombudsman’s jurisdiction and those that the respective state associations should address first. The move came after several members, including representatives of the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA), Kerala Cricket Association (KCA), Baroda Cricket Association (BCA), Punjab Cricket Association and Odisha Cricket Association (OCA), raised strong objections during the BCCI's Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai last week to the Ombudsman entertaining complaints related to local state matters.The members argued that such complaints lead to additional legal costs for the state associations and maintained that local grievance-redressal mechanisms should be exhausted before an issue is taken to the BCCI Ombudsman. They also questioned the Ombudsman's jurisdiction over matters that are primarily related to the functioning of individual state associations.Under the new framework, the Ombudsman will be provided with clear terms of reference governing the complaints it can entertain, particularly those relating to state associations."The BCCI will frame a policy that will curb the Ombudsman's interference in state-level matters. The board has decided to provide the Ombudsman with clear terms of reference when it comes to entertaining complaints related to state associations," an administrator who was part of the AGM told TimesofIndia.com.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
